(By Sri. V.Shrihari Naidu, Adv.)
 Judgment
This petition under Section 166 MV act is filed seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- for the injuries sustained by the Petitioner in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated that on 31-08-2021 at about 10.15 a.m., the Petitioner was rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-50-EF-2895 at Telecom Layout 4th Cross junction, Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03-ND-0352 (hereinafter called as offending vehicle)
drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Honda Activa scooter and accident occurred.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
She was immediately taken to Suraksha Health Care and Diagnostics Hospital, wherein she was treated as an inpatient and treated conservatively.

entities.text: Suraksha Health Care and Diagnostics Hospital
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Due to the accidental injuries, she is suffering from permanent disability and is unable to lead normal life as earlier.
It is claimed that the Petitioner has spent Rs.1,00,000/- for treatment, medicines, conveyance and other charges.

At the time of accident,
Petitioner was aged 26 years, working as an Executive Officer at SBI Cap and drawing salary of Rs.14,500/- per month.
Due to accidental injuries, she has lost her earning capacity and income.
As the accident was caused due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle, it is requested to award compensation from the Respondent No.1- Insured and Respondent No.2-Insurer.
3. In response to the petition notice, the Respondent No.1 and 2 have appeared before the court through their counsel and filed their separate written statements.

4. The respondent no.1 has denied all the averments of the petition inter-alia contending that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to negligent riding on the part of the petitioner.
The offending vehicle was insured with the respondent No.2 and policy was valid as on the date of accident and the driver was holding valid DL and has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

5. The respondent no.2 has filed its written statement and admitted the issuance of policy to the alleged offending vehicle and the liability if any is subject to the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
Further, denied the contents of petition averments in toto.

It has contended that the alleged accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, on the other hand, the accident has occurred due to sole negligence on the part of the rider (petitioner) of motorcycle.
It has contended that the petition is bad for non-joinder of necessary parties as the owner and insurer of motorcycle were not arrayed as respondents in the petition.
Further, it has contended that the petitioner was not wearing helmet and not holding DL at the time of accident.
Further, the driver of offending vehicle was not having valid DL as on the date of accident and concerned police have filed charge sheet in this regard.

It has also denied the nature of injuries sustained by the Petitioner, avocation and income of the Petitioner, and the future expenses claimed by her, expenses incurred by her and disability suffered by her.

Further contended that the Triveni S.N vs Dr. Shylaja.K.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128845723/
2 compensation claimed is highly exorbitant, excessive and unreasonable.
For all these, it has prayed for dismissal of the petition.

6. On the basis of the above pleadings, the following Issues were framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioner proves that she sustained injuries when she was riding the motorcycle bearing No.KA-50-EF-2895 on 31-08-2021 at about 10.15 a.m. near 4th Cross Junction, Telecom Layout, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Car bearing No.KA- 03-ND-0352??

2. What compensation Petitioner is entitled ?
3. What order ?

7. In order to prove the claim, the Petitioner examined herself as PW.1 and got marked the documents as per Ex.P.1 to P.13.
8.

Respondent No.2 has examined its official as RW-1 and got marked the documents at Ex.R.1 to 3.
9.

By considering the available materials on record and the arguments addressed by the parties, I have answered the above Issues as under:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.
Issue No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Issue No.3: As per the final order, for the following:
REASONS 10.
ISSUE NO.1:-

The case of the petitioner is that on 31-08-2021 at about 10.15 a.m., she was rider of Honda Activa scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-50-EF- 2895 at Telecom Layout 4th Cross junction,
Bengaluru, at that time, the driver of Car bearing Reg.No.KA-03- ND-0352 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Honda Activa scooter and accident occurred.
Due to the accident, Petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

11. In order to substantiate her case, petitioner has examined as PW-1 and got marked the police documents at Ex.P.1 to 7 i.e., FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, spot sketch, IMV report, wound certificate, and charge sheet.
As per wound certificate petitioner has sustained lacerated injury to face, hairline fracture in mandibular bone and abrasion to both knee joint.
12. The respondent No.2 has contended that the vehicle of the petitioner has not sustained any injuries.

The petitioner was riding her vehicle with out following the traffic rules and regulation and the alleged accident occurred due to the sole negligence of the petitioner and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of offending vehicle.
He has also taken contention that at time of accident petitioner was not wearing helmet and was not having effective driving licence.

Triveni S.N vs Dr. Shylaja.K.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128845723/
3 13.
Keeping in view of the arguments addressed by the learned counsel for the respondent once again I have perused the material available on record.

However on perusal of the charge sheet,
complaint and FIR, prima-facie establish that the accident occurred due to the negligence on the part of driver of the offending vehicle and not on the part of petitioner.
Neither the respondent has challenged the charge sheet before any authority nor rebut the evidence lead by the petitioner.
14. By looking into the oral and documentary evidence it is clear that accident occurred due to the negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
It is well settled principle that Motor Vehicles Act is beneficial legislation, the tribunal need not to go for the strict proof of rash and negligence.
There is no materials to disbelieve or rebut the evidence of the petitioner.
and charge sheet has been filed against the offending vehicle.
Therefore, this tribunal concludes that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
Thereby the accident occurred and petitioner has sustained injuries in a RTA.
Hence, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
15. ISSUE NO.2 :- As discussed in issue No.1 that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
So far as quantum of compensation is concerned the Petitioner has stated that she has spent more than 70,000/- towards treatment, medical, food and conveyance and other incidental expenses.

It is found that the Petitioner has sustained Lacerated injury to face with Hair line fracture in mandibular and abrasion to both knee joint as per Ex.P.6-wound certificate and doctor opined that the injury is simple in nature.
She has stated that she has spent Rs.70,000/- towards medical expenses and was working as an Executive Officer at SBI Cap and drawing salary of Rs.14,500/-p.m.
In support her avocation, income she has not produced any documents.

Moreover,
it is also not proved that due to the accidental injuries she is suffering from difficulties and is unable to work as earlier.
She has not examined the doctor to prove the permanent disability suffered by her.
Absolutely there is no disability stated and there is no evidence that the injury has affected her day to day activities.

She has produced the discharge summary at Ex.P.8 which shows that she was inpatient at Suraksha Health care and Diagnostics, Bengaluru from 31-8-2021 to 02-09- 2021 and also produced medical bills at Ex.P.10 amounting to Rs.67,550/-.

entities.text: Suraksha Health care and Diagnostics, Bengaluru
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Considering the nature of injury,
treatment taken by Petitioner, her age and the date of accident, I deem it proper to award .80,000/- of global compensation under all the conventional heads, as the Petitioner has suffered some sort of pain and had to take treatment for her injuries.

16. Liability: The Respondent no 2-insurance company has denied its liability only on the ground that the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident and it was the violation of the condition of the policy.
17.
Respondent No.1 RC owner has not contested the case by producing her driving licence.
Insurance company examined its official as RW-1.
Charge sheet filed against the driver of the offending for the offence punishable under section 279,338,IPC section 181 IMV Act.
Ex P7 establishes that driver of offending vehicle was not holding DL at time of the accident.

IO has issued issued notice U/s.133 of MV Act and obtained reply at EX R2 and R3.
18.
RW-1 has deposed that the Insurance company is not liable to pay compensation in view of violation of terms of insurance contract.

Triveni S.N vs Dr. Shylaja.K.S on 9 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128845723/
4 19.
In the present case admittedly insurance covers the third party risk.
The insurance policy is a contract executed between the owner and the insurer.
In the present case though the insurance was valid as on the date of accident, the respondent no 1 drove her car knowingly that she did not possess any valid driving licence.
It is the willful breach of terms of contract of insurance.

20. The learned counsel for the Respondent no 2 has relied upon the following decisions:
1. MFA.3297/2019 - Smt Adilakshmammama and others Vs. Sri Raju and others 21.

entities.text: MFA.3297/2019 - Smt Adilakshmammama and others Vs. Sri Raju and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: By considering the above said Judgment and the available materials on record, and since it is the third party liability, First Respondent RC owner is held liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

However, the 2nd respondent- insurance company i.e. insurer of the offending vehicle is directed to pay the compensation and recover the same from the owner i.e., Respondent No.1 in view of breach of contract of insurance.
With these observation I answer Issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

22. ISSUE NO.3 : In view of the above discussion, reasons stated and findings given to Issue Nos.1 &
2, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER Claim Petition filed under Sec.166 of M.V.Act is allowed in part with cost.

Petitioner is awarded compensation of Rs.80,000/- together with interest @ 6% p.a.
from the date of petition till the date of deposit with the Tribunal.
Respondent No.1-RC owner is liable to pay the above compensation to the Petitioner.

Respondent No.2 shall deposit aforesaid amount within two months from the date of this order and recover the entire compensation amount along with interest from the Respondent No.1 in view of violation of terms of policy.
After deposit of the compensation amount, entire amount with interest shall be disbursed to the petitioner through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at .1,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly on computer, corrected, signed and pronounced by me in open court dated this the 9th day of January 2025.)
(SHYLA S.M.) II Addl. Judge & ACJM Member, MACT, Court of Small Causes, Bengaluru.
